input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 selects New York law, which is our preferred governing law, but the Agreement contains no venue, jurisdiction or arbitration provision anywhere (searches for court, jurisdiction and arbitration return nothing). Because no forum is designated, the preferred position's exclusive-jurisdiction element fails, and the fallback (Delaware/California/England and Wales law with corresponding courts) is not met either. We therefore add a single venue sentence fixing exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere, leaving the governing law sentence untouched.

ops.text: Venue. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York over the merits of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction.
